(CNN)  -- Authorities searched a church near where an 8-year-old California girl was found dead Monday in the hopes of finding clues that would lead to her killer. Mourners leave condolences for Sandra Cantu, who was found dead on April 6 in Tracy, California. The body of Sandra Cantu of Tracy, California, was found stuffed into a suitcase in a dairy-farm pond. Cantu had been missing since March 27. Tracy police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN's Nancy Grace he would not elaborate on what evidence led them to Clover Road Baptist Church. He would say only that detectives developed probable cause that persuaded a judge to sign a search warrant. Lane Lawless, the church's pastor, told CNN affiliate KCRA he was questioned for about three hours by police, adding that he had nothing to do with Cantu's disappearance or death. "We have fully cooperated with the police," Lawless told KCRA. "We have answered all their questions." Authorities also searched the mobile home park Tuesday where the girl lived.  Watch report on murder investigation » . "Investigators are looking at additional information they received since yesterday (Monday) and, hopefully, that will lead us to Sandra's killers," Sheneman said. Asked if his use of the plural meant police were looking for more than one person, Sheneman responded, "We have no specific suspects."  Watch Sheneman say there has not been an arrest in the case » . Sheneman also implied the killer likely was familiar with the location where the body was found. He said he himself was unfamiliar with the location where the girl's body was found, despite having lived in the community for nearly 12 years. "Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there," he said.  Watch how the suitcase was found » . Sheneman said police had no one in custody, despite having interviewed hundreds of people regarding the case. "Everyone that we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest," he said. "We're not eliminating anyone." The autopsy was being conducted Tuesday, but it was not clear when the report would be available. "It's going to be some time before we hear from the coroner," Sheneman said. "I can't tell you when that's going to be." More than 10 search warrants have been executed as part of the investigation and "a lot" of evidence has been recovered, Sheneman said. The day Cantu was last reported seen, she returned home from school, kissed her mother and left to play with a friend who lives nearby. A short time later, wearing a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings, she left to go to another friend's home, according to a family spokeswoman. Police said Monday the girl's clothing helped them identify the body.

outputs.L1:
(CNN) — Authorities searched a church near the site where an 8-year-old California girl was found dead Monday, hoping to uncover clues that could lead them to her killer.

Mourners have left condolences for Sandra Cantu, who was found dead on April 6 in Tracy, California. Sandra Cantu’s body was discovered stuffed inside a suitcase in a dairy-farm pond. She had been missing since March 27.

Tracy Police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN’s Nancy Grace that he would not elaborate on what evidence led investigators to Clover Road Baptist Church. He said only that detectives had developed probable cause, which persuaded a judge to sign a search warrant.

Lane Lawless, the church’s pastor, told CNN affiliate KCRA that police questioned him for about three hours. He added that he had nothing to do with Cantu’s disappearance or death.

“We have fully cooperated with the police,” Lawless told KCRA. “We have answered all their questions.”

Authorities also searched the mobile home park Tuesday where the girl lived.

“Investigators are looking at additional information they received since yesterday [Monday] and, hopefully, that will lead us to Sandra’s killers,” Sheneman said.

Asked whether his use of the plural meant police were looking for more than one person, Sheneman responded, “We have no specific suspects.”

Sheneman also suggested that the killer was likely familiar with the location where the body was found. He said he himself was unfamiliar with the site, despite having lived in the community for nearly 12 years.

“Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there,” he said.

Sheneman said police had no one in custody, despite having interviewed hundreds of people in connection with the case.

“Everyone that we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest,” he said. “We’re not eliminating anyone.”

An autopsy was being conducted Tuesday, though it was unclear when the report would be available.

“It’s going to be some time before we hear from the coroner,” Sheneman said. “I can’t tell you when that’s going to be.”

More than 10 search warrants have been executed as part of the investigation, and “a lot” of evidence has been recovered, Sheneman said.

On the day Cantu was last reported seen, she returned home from school, kissed her mother, and left to play with a friend who lived nearby. A short time later, wearing a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings, she left to go to another friend’s home, according to a family spokeswoman.

Police said Monday that the girl’s clothing helped them identify the body.

(CNN) — Investigators searched a church located near the area where the body of 8-year-old Sandra Cantu was discovered Monday, hoping to uncover evidence that could help identify whoever killed her.

Sandra Cantu, from Tracy, California, had been missing since March 27. Her body was found April 6 inside a suitcase in a pond on a dairy farm in Tracy. Mourners later left messages of sympathy for the girl.

Tracy police Sgt. Tony Sheneman told CNN’s Nancy Grace that he would not discuss the specific evidence that brought investigators to Clover Road Baptist Church. He said only that detectives had established probable cause, which convinced a judge to approve a search warrant.

The church’s pastor, Lane Lawless, told CNN affiliate KCRA that police questioned him for roughly three hours. He said he had no involvement in Cantu’s disappearance or death.

“We have fully cooperated with the police,” Lawless told KCRA. “We have answered all their questions.”

On Tuesday, investigators also searched the mobile home park where Cantu lived.

Sheneman said investigators were reviewing new information received since Monday and hoped it would help lead them to Sandra’s killer or killers. When asked whether his use of the plural suggested police believed more than one person might be involved, he answered, “We have no specific suspects.”

Sheneman also suggested that the person responsible probably knew the area where Cantu’s body was located. Although he had lived in the community for almost 12 years, he said he was not familiar with that particular spot.

“Someone would have to be familiar with that area to know to go there,” he said.

Police had interviewed hundreds of people in connection with the investigation, Sheneman said, but no one had been arrested or taken into custody.

“Everyone that we speak to right now is being considered a person of interest,” he said. “We’re not eliminating anyone.”

An autopsy was under way Tuesday, though officials did not know when the findings would be released.

“It’s going to be some time before we hear from the coroner,” Sheneman said. “I can't tell you when that's going to be.”

According to Sheneman, investigators had carried out more than 10 search warrants and recovered “a lot” of evidence.

On the day Cantu was last seen, she came home from school, kissed her mother, and went out to play with a nearby friend. Soon afterward, wearing a pink Hello Kitty T-shirt and black leggings, she headed to another friend’s house, a family spokeswoman said.

Police said Monday that the clothing helped them confirm the body was Cantu’s.

Sandra was reported missing on **March 27, 2009**, after she was last seen near the **Orchard Estates Mobile Home Park** in Tracy, where she lived with her family. Surveillance footage from the mobile-home community showed the girl walking near her home that afternoon, but she did not return. Her disappearance prompted an extensive search involving law enforcement, volunteers, divers, search dogs and local residents.

After more than a week of searching, investigators made a grim discovery on **April 6, 2009**: Sandra’s body was found inside a suitcase submerged in an irrigation pond on or near a dairy farm outside Tracy. Authorities treated the case as a homicide and began focusing on people connected to the mobile-home park and the child’s daily life.

The investigation soon led to **Melissa Huckaby**, a woman who lived in the same mobile-home park and was known to Sandra’s family. Huckaby was the granddaughter of a local pastor and had taught Sunday school, facts that intensified public shock in the close-knit community. Police arrested Huckaby on **April 10, 2009**, after interviews and evidence tied her to the case.

Prosecutors charged Huckaby with Sandra’s murder, along with special circumstances including kidnapping. Authorities said Sandra had been taken from the area where she lived before her body was later placed in the pond. Investigators did not publicly establish a clear motive, and many details of the crime were kept limited because of the child’s age and the sensitivity of the case.

In **2010**, Huckaby pleaded guilty to **first-degree murder** with a special circumstance allegation, avoiding a trial. She was sentenced to **life in prison without the possibility of parole**. During court proceedings, Sandra’s family and community members described the devastating impact of the crime and the loss of a child remembered as lively, affectionate and full of personality.

Sandra Cantu’s death left a lasting mark on Tracy, a San Joaquin County city where residents had joined together in the hope of finding her alive. The case remains one of the region’s most widely remembered child homicide cases, both for the intense search that followed her disappearance and for the betrayal felt when the person convicted was someone from within the child’s own community.
